label: Claude Sonnet 5.5
output:
**Title: One star for now: good software, support that disappeared after we signed**

I'm the director of Bridger Bend Community Library, a one-branch library in Montana with two full-time staff, a crew of volunteers, and about 2,300 active cardholders. We signed a three-year, $14,200-a-year contract with Stackhouse Cloud in June, and our catalog and circulation went live on the platform on October 19.

I want to be fair about what's good. The demo was accurate, and the staff interface is better than the system it replaced. My complaint is not with the product idea. It's with what happens when something goes wrong.

Since October 28, checkouts have only worked offline on a single laptop, and our holds queue was wiped. About 640 holds are gone. Our support ticket has been open 12 days. I've had three replies, and every one said the issue was "escalated to engineering." No timeline, no workaround, no name.

During the sales process we were promised a dedicated migration specialist. What we got was a shared inbox.

Here is what that means in a town our size. A retired rancher drove 40 minutes for a set of large-print Westerns he'd been waiting on. We had no record of his hold, and he went home empty-handed. Meanwhile, a volunteer is writing checkouts on index cards. Our budget hearing with the county is November 18, and this line item is on the agenda. I'd rather be explaining a success.

I'm giving one star for now. I'll gladly revisit it if this gets fixed.

I'm asking for a named, senior person at Stackhouse to call me this week with a real recovery plan and a date for restoring our holds and online circulation.

To other directors weighing Stackhouse, especially small libraries without an IT department: before you sign, ask for these in writing.

- Guaranteed support response and resolution times
- The name of your actual migration contact, and what happens if that person is unavailable
- What the rollback or data-recovery plan is if holds or circulation data are lost

A good product doesn't help much when nobody picks up the phone.

*Director, Bridger Bend Community Library*

---

I wrote the call as a request, since I wasn't sure whether someone had already committed to phoning you. If a named person has confirmed, tell me and I'll swap in their name and make that line firmer. This comes to roughly 330 words.
